A violin plot shows the **full shape of a distribution** — where the density is thick or thin —
instead of collapsing it to a box's quartiles. And when you want to compare two conditions at the
same position, a **split (half) violin** puts one condition on each half. Here we build both in R
with [canvasXpress](https://canvasxpress.org): interactive, and reproducible because the figure is
one portable spec.

## The data

A measurement across a few dose groups and two conditions. Swap in your own long-format table.

```{r}
#| message: false
library(canvasXpress)

set.seed(1)
doses <- c("Low", "Medium", "High"); conds <- c("Control", "Treated")
value <- c(); Dose <- c(); Condition <- c()
for (d in doses) for (co in conds) {
  mu <- if (d == "Low") 6 else if (d == "Medium") 8 else 10
  if (co == "Treated") mu <- mu + 1.5
  value <- c(value, round(rnorm(40, mu, 1.2), 2))
  Dose <- c(Dose, rep(d, 40)); Condition <- c(Condition, rep(co, 40))
}
```

In canvasXpress terms a violin is a `Boxplot` graph with the violin turned on: one measured variable
× N observations, with the grouping columns as `smpAnnot`.

```{r}
ids <- paste0("o", seq_along(value))
y <- data.frame(matrix(value, nrow = 1, dimnames = list("value", ids)), check.names = FALSE)
smpAnnot <- data.frame(Dose = Dose, Condition = Condition, row.names = ids, check.names = FALSE)
```

## A full violin per group

`showViolinBoxplot = TRUE` draws the violin (with a small boxplot inside); `violinScale = "area"`
makes equal-area violins.

```{r}
canvasXpress(
  data = y, smpAnnot = smpAnnot, graphType = "Boxplot",
  showViolinBoxplot = TRUE, violinScale = "area",
  groupingFactors = list("Dose"), xAxis = list("value"),
  smpTitle = "Dose", title = "Distribution of value by dose",
  width = 650, height = 500
)
```

## A split (half) violin comparing two conditions

Group by **both** factors, colour by the condition, and set `violinSide = "split"` — the two
conditions share each dose position, one on each half. This reads far better than two full violins
side by side.

```{r}
canvasXpress(
  data = y, smpAnnot = smpAnnot, graphType = "Boxplot",
  showViolinBoxplot = TRUE, violinScale = "area",
  groupingFactors = list("Dose", "Condition"), colorBy = "Condition",
  violinSide = "split", violinTrim = FALSE, xAxis = list("value"),
  smpTitle = "Dose", title = "Control vs Treated — split violin by dose",
  width = 650, height = 500
)
```

Hover to read the density and summary stats. `violinSide` can also be `"lt"` or `"rb"` for a
one-sided half violin (handy for a raincloud when paired with `violinPointsSide`).

## Why "reproducible"

The `data`+`config` **is** the figure — one portable JSON spec that renders the identical violins
from Python or JavaScript, and can be validated and re-rendered later.
